answer: Contention probes catch clones that share one machine. Auditors pick a random set of identities and send each a heavy compute task at the same moment, with a tight deadline. Separate agents finish on time; twenty clones on one server must split its cores, so replies slow in a spiral as the queue backs up, and the auditors' board shades that set umber for review. Each extra identity therefore needs its own reserved hardware as an anchor, which erases the profit of splitting. Limitation: rented burst capacity can mask contention, and honest agents on shared hosts need appeals.
